title: Colour Modes and Theming
summary: Bootstrap 5.3 can use light or dark colours. A theme setting chooses which set of colours a page part uses.
introduction: Bootstrap 5.3 can use light or dark colours. A theme setting chooses which set of colours a page part uses. Try a small card in each theme. Check that words, borders and focus marks are still easy to see.
learningObjectives: Enable dark mode for a page or one component with data-bs-theme
Build a light and dark toggle that respects the system preference
Use Bootstrap's CSS variables to retheme colours without Sass
Choose colour-mode-aware classes so components stay readable in both modes

blocks.text: The 5.3 stylesheet defines two sets of root variables: one for light mode, on `:root` and `[data-bs-theme="light"]`, and one for dark mode, on `[data-bs-theme="dark"]`. Components never hard-code a colour; a card reads `--bs-body-bg`, a border reads `--bs-border-color`, an alert reads `--bs-success-bg-subtle`. Set the attribute on `<html>` and every variable, and therefore every component, flips at once. Bootstrap does **not** watch the operating system setting by itself; you either set the attribute or, as the toggle below does, read the system preference with JavaScript.

blocks.code:

Everything below adapts without extra classes.

Opens at dusk and closes by morning.

blocks.title: Rendered result
blocks.content:
Page background #212529 with light grey (#dee2e6) text
The card shares the dark background and has a mid-grey border; its button is the same blue as in light mode
The alert is dark green with pale green text, the reverse of its light-mode colours

blocks.text: Remove the attribute and the same markup renders in light mode. That is the whole point: the components did not change, only the variables they read.

Because the dark variables are defined on `[data-bs-theme="dark"]` rather than on `html` alone, the attribute works on **any** element and applies to everything inside it. A dark footer or navbar on an otherwise light page is one attribute, and the links, borders and form controls inside it recolour themselves.

blocks.title: Rendered result
blocks.content: A #212529 footer with light grey text and a light blue (#6ea8fe) link, while the rest of the page keeps its white background and dark text

blocks.text: A toggle that remembers the choice

A good toggle does three things: on first visit it follows the operating system (`prefers-color-scheme`), it stores the user's explicit choice, and it applies the stored choice *before* the page paints so there is no flash of the wrong theme. That last point is why the first script sits in the `<head>` and is tiny. The button handler can live at the end of the body as usual.

blocks.code: Theme toggle

blocks.title: Behaviour in the browser
blocks.content:
First visit on a system set to dark: the page loads dark immediately, with no light flash
Clicking "Switch theme" flips the whole page between light and dark
After a reload the page comes back in whichever mode was chosen last, regardless of the system setting

blocks.text: The same variables are your theming API. Override them in a stylesheet loaded **after** Bootstrap, once for light mode and once for dark mode when the values differ. Root variables control page-wide things such as the font stack, body background and link colour; links in 5.3 are built from `--bs-link-color-rgb`, so override the `-rgb` variants. Components have their own prefixed variables, for example `--bs-btn-bg` on buttons, which you set on the component's class.

blocks.title: Place after the Bootstrap stylesheet link
Rendered result
blocks.content:
Light mode: cream page background, serif text, dark red links that darken on hover; primary buttons are dark red and darken on hover and press
Dark mode: near-black page background with the same serif text; the buttons keep their dark red

blocks.title: Common mistake: changing --bs-primary and expecting buttons to follow
blocks.text: `--bs-primary` is informational: `btn-primary`, `bg-primary` and `text-primary` do not read it. Buttons use `--bs-btn-bg` and friends, which were compiled from the Sass variable `$primary` into fixed values; backgrounds use `--bs-primary-rgb`. Overriding only `--bs-primary` therefore changes nothing visible. Set the component variables as above, or change `$primary` in Sass (next lesson) to recolour everything at once.

Some utilities are fixed colours and some follow the mode. Choose the adaptive ones wherever a page might be viewed dark, and keep the fixed ones for things that must stay the same, such as a brand bar.

blocks.title: Invent your own mode
blocks.text: Nothing limits the attribute to light and dark. A rule for `[data-bs-theme="sepia"]` that sets `--bs-body-bg`, `--bs-body-color` and a few others gives you a third mode that every component honours, selectable with the same toggle code.

questions.question: Out of the box, Bootstrap 5.3 switches to dark mode automatically when the operating system is set to dark.
questions.explanation: The CDN build only reacts to the data-bs-theme attribute. Reading prefers-color-scheme and setting the attribute is your script's job, unless you rebuild Bootstrap with $color-mode-type set to media-query.

questions.question: Which background class changes colour when the page switches to dark mode?
questions.explanation: bg-body-tertiary reads a colour-mode variable (light grey in light mode, dark grey in dark mode). bg-light, bg-white and bg-secondary are fixed colours.
